after its own `midi.list_inputs` command. Only on a session.

`error` `midi.connect` when it cannot open. The page sends it after its own
`midi.select_input` command. Only on a session.

Where the helper's MIDI input plays its notes (#598): the engine slots of the tracks
the live input reaches now (`commands::live::input_targets`: the selected track and the
armed MIDI tracks), in the engine `epoch` whose slots they are
(`commands::host::LiveRouting`). The page sends it after each snapshot it sends and
whenever the table changes. The helper plays each note of its input on these tracks at
once, in this epoch, and its note off on the tracks the note went to; a table of
another epoch than its engine's is ignored, and so is one longer than the engine's
track limit. Only on a session.

The page's answer to the helper's `agent.call` of the same `id` (AG-1): what running
the agent's command did. The helper takes it only from the link (session or control
link) the call went to. On a session or a control link.

The page came to the front (shown, or focused) (#608): its control link becomes the one
the agents' calls go to while no session is greeted, so with several pages open an agent
drives the one the user last looked at. Only on a control link.

Start a new project: the page's default one, a single synth track, in no folder yet,
with its own identity. It replaces the current project, its history and its session
(the chosen MIDI input stays); the engine starts over from it. Not undoable, destructive:
the page first keeps the current project's changes where it can (written into its folder,
or kept as a draft in the browser's storage, which stays listed). Only when they cannot
be kept anywhere does it ask the user, whoever sends the command, and nothing changes if
the user cancels. The question is a dialog of the page, so it needs no click. `name`
is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters): without one the project is called
"Sketch" (the page names its drafts by the time they were started, #473).

catalog.description:
Write the project to its folder now, without waiting for the automatic save that
follows each change by a moment. A project that has no folder yet asks for one, as
`project.save_as` does. Changes nothing in the project, so it never enters the
history.
catalog.name: project.save

catalog.description:
Ask the user for the project's name (a field prefilled with the current one), then for
a folder, and write the whole project into a folder of that name inside it; the project
takes that name (a `project.rename`, undoable) and then lives in that folder, and the
automatic save keeps writing there. The name and the folder are chosen by the user (a
browser needs a click for it), so an agent that is not driven by one gets a notice in the
page instead, and nothing is chosen. A folder of that name that already holds files is
refused. The old folder is left as it is. Changes nothing else in the project, so the save
itself never enters the history.
catalog.name: project.save_as

catalog.description:
Export the project as a `.faulkpack`, a zip of its folder that any Faulk reads back,
and hand it to the user as a download. It holds the project as it is now, saved or
not, and the media the project refers to. This is how a project kept in the browser
(no folder chosen) is backed up or moved. Changes nothing in the project, so it never
enters the history.
catalog.name: project.export_pack

catalog.description:
Open a `.faulkpack` the user chooses: its project replaces the current one and is kept
in the browser as a new project of its own (an import never overwrites a project that
is already there). A file is chosen by the user (a browser needs a click for it), so
an agent that is not driven by one gets a notice in the page instead. A file that is
not a valid pack is refused with the reason and nothing changes. The history of the
replaced project is gone; the page asks first when that project has changes that are
not kept anywhere.
catalog.name: project.import_pack

catalog.description:
Open a `.faulkpack` hosted at `url`: `https`, with no user name or password in it (plain
`http` only to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, and the page takes it only when Faulk
itself runs on this computer). The page downloads it without cookies or credentials,
checks it whole (size, files, format) and opens its project as a new project of its own,
as `project.import_pack` does with a file: kept in the browser's storage where the
browser has one, in the tab alone where it has none. Nothing in the pack runs as code.
When the browser already keeps the project of that pack (the same link opened before), the
page opens the copy it keeps instead of a second one. The current project is never
overwritten: it stays where it is kept (its folder, or the browser), and
`project.list_stored` then `project.open_browser_project` or `project.open_recent` bring
it back; the page asks first when that project has changes that are kept nowhere. A link
that cannot be downloaded, a file that is not a valid pack and a pack that is too big are
refused in the page with a notice, and nothing changes. The result only says the command
was accepted, not how the download ended. Not undoable: opening a project is not an edit
of one; go back to the previous project through the project list.
catalog.name: project.open_url

and the projects kept in the browser's own storage (each with a `dir`), newest first.
The page reads its storage again before it answers. The `id` and the `dir` are the
names `project.open_recent`, `project.open_browser_project` and
`project.delete_browser_project` take. Changes nothing in the project.

and could not (locked by another tab, unreadable): the notice then offers this command
as its retry. A folder still needs the user's click when the browser withdrew its
permission: an agent that is not driven by one gets a notice in the page. Nothing
happens, with a notice, when the page offers nothing. The current project is replaced;
the page asks first when it has changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces
the history.

chosen by the user (a browser needs a click for it), so an agent that is not driven by

the reason and nothing changes. The page asks first when the current project has
changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces the history.
catalog.name: project.open_folder

replacing the current project. When the browser withdrew its permission on the folder,

a notice in the page. An `id` the page does not know is refused with a notice. The page
asks first when the current project has changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it
replaces the history.

catalog.description:

has no folders), by the `dir` that `project.list_stored` gives, replacing the current

that another tab has open. The page asks first when the current project has changes
that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces the history.

catalog.description:

`project.list_stored` gives. The page always asks the user to confirm first, whoever
sends the command, and nothing is deleted until the user says yes. The project that is
open, a project another tab has open and a `dir` the page does not list are refused
with a notice. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user
answered. Not undoable: the files are gone (`project.export_pack` makes a copy first).

catalog.description:

changes, keep this page's version: the folder's files are replaced by the project right
away, and the outside edits are lost. The page always asks the user to
confirm first, whoever sends the command. Refused with a notice when the folder is not
in conflict. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user answered.
Changes nothing in the project, so it never enters the history.

changes, take the folder's version: the project is replaced by what the folder holds,
and the changes made since the last write are lost. The page always asks the user to
confirm first, whoever sends the command. Refused with a notice when the folder is not
in conflict. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user answered.
Not undoable: it replaces the history.

catalog.description:
Measure how loud the song is without playing it nor writing a file: the same
offline render as `project.export_audio` (the engine that plays the song, run
faster than real time), but only the levels come back, per track and for the
master, so an agent without ears learns whether its song sounds, whether it is too
loud, and whether a track is silent. The range is the whole song by default, or
bars `from_bar` to `to_bar` (both, counted from 1, the last one included); the
tail after the range is not measured. Levels are in dBFS (0 is full scale), `null`
is silence; a peak is the larger of the two channels, an RMS the power mean of
both, over the whole range (not the loudest short window that `mixer.levels`
gives). The metronome and the loop are off, the solo and mute state are on. Audio
clips are measured as they play: the render reads their files from the project's
folder, and a file that cannot be read leaves its clip silent. Refused, as an export
is, when there is nothing to render (empty arrangement, a range that starts after
the end of the arrangement or is out of order), and when the range lasts more than
10 minutes (a `limit` error). The page runs the render in the background (a few
seconds for a few minutes of music), one at a time; it answers `unavailable` when
another analysis runs or the page's engine is not ready. A query: changes nothing
in the project and never enters the history.
catalog.name: project.analyze_render

catalog.description:
Render the project to an audio file (WAV) and save it, offline: the same engine
that plays the song, run faster than real time, so the file is the song as it
sounds, not a recording of the speakers. `region` is `song` (default: from bar 1
to the end of the last placement of the arrangement, then the tail, so that an
effect such as the echo rings out; the file ends where the sound falls under
-90 dBFS, after 30 seconds at most), `loop` (the loop region once, then the same
tail) or `bars` (from the start of bar `from_bar` to the end of bar `to_bar`, both
counted from 1, required with it and refused without it, the last one included,
then the same tail). `bit_depth` is `pcm16`, `pcm24` (default) or `float32`;
`sample_rate` is 44100, 48000 (default) or 96000. The metronome is never in the
file; the solo and mute state are. Audio clips are in the file as they play: the
render reads their files from the project's folder, in the page in both modes (so in
Boost too, where they are not heard yet), and waits for each read; a file that cannot
be read leaves its clips silent and the page names it when the render ends. It is
refused when there is
nothing to render (empty arrangement, no loop region for `loop`, a `bars` range that
starts after the end of the arrangement or is out of order) or the range lasts more
than 30 minutes
(a `limit` error). The output says what will be rendered; the page runs the render, shows its progress and asks
where to save the file (a folder picker needs a click), so an agent that is not
driven by a user gets the render in the page to confirm. Changes nothing in the
project, so it never enters the history and has nothing to undo.

catalog.description:
Move placements to other MIDI tracks, in one command and one history entry, and
optionally in time too (`by` ticks, default 0, negative is earlier). `moves` pairs
each placement with the track it ends in (its own track keeps it there): a selection
of several tracks can move one track down together, each clip to its own target.
The clip of a moved placement goes with it: the target track gets a copy of the
clip (one copy per source clip and target track, so placements that were linked and
move together stay linked; same name, colour, length, loop and notes, not in the
launch grid), and a source clip left with no placement and no grid slot is removed
from its track (a clip in the grid, or one still placed elsewhere, stays). The
moved placements get new identifiers in another track (`placements`, in the order of
`moves`) and keep their length and offset; they win on overlap in the target (the
placements they cover are carved, `overwritten` counts them). Refused when `moves`
is empty, names a placement twice or an unknown one, names an unknown track or one
that is not a MIDI track (audio clips come from import), when a placement is an
audio one, when one would start before tick 0 or end past 2^40, or on a limit.
Nothing moves (and no history entry is made) when every placement stays in its
track and `by` is 0. Undo: `arrangement.restore`, which puts the placements and the
removed clips back with their identifiers and removes the copies.

catalog.description:
Insert `length` ticks of empty time at the timeline tick `at`, in every track and in
the master, in one history entry (bar-level editing: a bar is 3840 ticks in 4/4).
A placement that starts at or after `at` moves `length` ticks later; one that
straddles `at` is split there, the right part (a new placement of the same clip, so
linked) moving later and resuming the clip where the left part stops, round the clip.
The points of every automation lane at or after `at` move too (a ramp that straddles
`at` stretches), so do the section markers at or after `at` (#473), and so do the
loop region's boundaries after `at` (a loop that contains `at` grows). Tempo and time
signature hold one point at tick 0 and do not move; the playhead and the launch grid
do not move. Refused with `invalid` when `at` is not in [0, 2^40], `length` is less
than 1 or the cut would pass 2^40, or when a placement or a point would pass 2^40,
and with `limit` when the splits pass the placement limits. Refused too, for the
whole project, while any track holds an audio placement (`clip.import_audio` into
the arrangement makes one): audio placements do not move in time yet. Changes nothing
(no history entry) when nothing lies at or after `at`. Undo: `arrangement.restore_time`.

catalog.description:
Delete the time `[from, to)` ticks from every track and from the master,
and close the gap, in one history entry. Placements are cut at both edges: what lies
inside is removed (a placement that straddles the whole range is split in two, the
right part a new placement resuming the clip where the range ends), what starts at or
after `to` moves `to - from` ticks earlier; a clip that loses its last placement stays
in its track's pool. The points of every automation lane inside the range are removed and the
later ones move back, so the last point before the cut links straight to the first
one after it (a `step` point keeps holding its value up to the cut, then the next
value applies: the lane is not smoothed). The section markers after the range move
back, one inside it goes to `from` (#473). The loop region follows (a boundary inside
the range falls to `from`;
a loop left empty is cleared and switched off). Tempo and time signature hold one
point at tick 0 and do not move; the playhead and the launch grid do not move.
Refused with `invalid` when `from` is not in [0, 2^40], `to` is not after `from` or
passes 2^40, and with `limit` when the cuts pass the placement limits. Refused too, for
the whole project, while any track holds an audio placement (audio placements do not
move in time yet). Changes nothing (no history entry) when nothing lies at or after
`from`. Undo:
`arrangement.restore_time`.

catalog.description:
Create an empty automation lane on a parameter of a track or of the master. Name the
owner with `track` (a track's identifier) or with `master: true` (the master),
exactly one of the two. `target` is
`{"device": {"device": <device id>, "param": <parameter key>}}` for a parameter of
one of the owner's devices (the keys are in the device descriptors of the schema
bundle; the device must be in the owner's chain: a track's, or the master's effects)
or `{"mixer": {"param": "gain"}}` / `{"mixer": {"param": "pan"}}` for the owner's
volume or pan (there is no mute lane). Refused with `not_found` for an unknown track,
for a device that is not in the owner's chain (another track's, or the master's for a
track's lane) or a parameter the device lacks, with `invalid` when both or neither of
`track` and `master` are given or when the owner already has a lane on that parameter,
and with `limit` at the safety limit of lanes.
A new lane has no point yet and has no effect on the sound until points are added
with `automation.points.add`: create the lane, then add its points. Once it has points,
it holds the first point's value from the start of the timeline until that point, and the engine applies
its value at the playhead when the transport stops and at every seek, so a lane with a
single point at bar 9 already sets its parameter from bar 1. A lane belongs to the
track, not to its clips. Undo: `automation.lane.delete`.

catalog.description:
Add points to a lane, in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing). Each point
is `{tick, value, shape}`: `tick` 0 to 2^40, `value` in the parameter's unit (rounded
to its step; a device parameter is clamped to its range, a gain outside -96..+6 dB or
a pan outside -1..1 is refused), `shape` `linear` (default) or `step`; a linear segment
of a volume lane is a straight line along the fader's travel (not in amplitude nor in
dB), of any other lane a straight line in its unit. A lane has at
most one point per tick: a tick that already holds a different point, or that appears
twice in the batch, is refused (use `automation.points.update` to change a point); a
point equal to the one already there changes nothing. Refused with `limit` past the
safety limit of points per lane or in the project. Before its first point a lane holds
the first point's value (from tick 0, bar 1), so the first point sets the value of
everything before it: to keep a parameter at its current value until a change, add a
point at tick 0 with that value. Points are at absolute ticks of the timeline, they do
not follow clips. Undo: `automation.points.remove` of the points actually added.

Id.description: A stable identifier: 26 characters of Crockford base32 (a ULID), generated by the project.

Point.description: A point of a lane, as the commands take and return it.

shape.description:
The transition from this point to the next: `linear` (default) or `step`. `linear`
is a straight line in the parameter's unit, except for a volume (`gain`) lane, where
it is a straight line along the travel of the mixer's fader, the same law as the
lane's axis (-96 dB, silence, at the bottom, 0 dB at 78 % of the travel, +6 dB at the
top): a fade from 0 dB to -96 dB goes down like a fader pulled at constant speed, and
half way is -21 dB, neither -6 dB (amplitude) nor -48 dB (dB). `step` holds the value.

value.description: The value, in the parameter's unit; rounded to its step.

Shape.description: The shape of the transition from a point to the next one.

catalog.description:
Read how loud the project sounds now, per track and for the master, from the
meters of the playing engine: how an agent without ears learns whether a song
sounds. Call it while the transport plays (`transport.play`): the meters keep the
largest peak and the loudest RMS since the previous call (at most the last 10
seconds), so a call right after a passage covers it. That RMS is the loudest of
the engine's short windows (about 30 ms), so it reads higher than the RMS of a
whole passage, which is what `project.analyze_render` gives. Levels are in dBFS (0 is
full scale; the master is measured before the output protection, so it can read
above 0), `null` is silence; a peak is the larger of the two channels, an RMS the
power mean of both. `playing` says whether the transport ran: when it did not (or
the audio is not started, or the engine has stopped reporting), every level is
`null`. Tracks come in display order, after their fader and mute. To measure a
stretch without playing it, use `project.analyze_render`. `silenced_frames` above 0
says the output protection silenced an invalid (non-finite) signal since the engine
started, which the levels cannot show. A query: changes nothing
and never enters the history.

Change the settings of recording; every field is optional and a field left out stays
as it is. `offset_ms` (-500 to 500): every recorded note is moved this much earlier,
on top of the output latency the host estimates (negative: later). `replace`: a take
removes, in the clip it writes into, the notes that start in the range it recorded
(from its first note to the end of its last), instead of adding to them (overdub,
the default). `quantize_on_input` (`none`, `quarter`, `eighth`, `sixteenth`,
`thirty-second`, `eighth-triplet`, `sixteenth-triplet`; default `none`) and
`quantize_strength` (0 to 100 percent, default 100): the starts of the take's own
notes are moved toward that grid of the clip when `record.commit_take` writes the
take, never the notes the clip already had, and never their lengths. They belong to
the machine, so they are session state: saved with the session, never in the
project, and not undoable. A take uses the settings at the moment it is written, unless `record.commit_take` is given its own.

catalog.description:
Start recording the armed MIDI tracks (`track.arm`); refused when none is armed or
when a take is still waiting to be committed. `target`: `{"at": "scene", "scene":
<id>}` (the launch grid: overdub into the cell's clip, or a new clip in an empty
cell) or `{"at": "arrangement"}` (the default: each note where it is played). From a
stopped transport it plays from the play position, after the metronome's count-in
bars (heard, not recorded), and with a scene target it launches that scene's clip
of each armed track first; on a running transport it records at once. `latency_ms`

catalog.description:
Write a take into the project, every track at once, as **one** history entry. Per
track, `notes` are the notes as played: `start` in transport ticks, `length` in
ticks. Every start is first moved `shift_ms` earlier at the project's tempo; when the
transport loops and the start is inside the loop, the move wraps round the loop (a note
that would go before the loop's start comes from its end). With a
scene target, a cell that holds a clip takes the notes on top of its own (overdub):
a note lands where the clip played at that moment, from `anchor` (the transport tick
of the clip's position 0) or else from the bar of the first note, round its loop;
a clip without a loop grows to the bar after the last note. An empty cell gets a new
clip from the bar of the first note to the bar after the last one (at least one
bar), looping over its length. With the arrangement target, a note inside a
placement goes into its clip where the placement shows it; the other notes make one
new clip per gap between placements, from the bar of its first note to the bar after
its last, cut at the next placement. A note before tick 0 or before its clip is
dropped and counted; a note longer than its clip is cut at the clip's end. With
`replace` on (`record.set_settings`), a clip that takes notes first loses the notes
that start in the range the track recorded (its first note to the end of its last),
counted in `replaced`. With `quantize_on_input` on, the starts of the take's notes
move toward the grid of their clip by `quantize_strength` (a note stays inside its
clip, lengths never change). Undo: `record.restore` puts the clips back as they
were, replaced notes included. `replace`, `quantize_on_input` and `quantize_strength`
override the session's settings (`record.set_settings`) for this write only; left out,
the session's apply.

ArrangementCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Put a clip of the track in the arrangement, as a new placement of the same clip
(a linked clip: editing the clip changes every placement of it); a clip of the
track's pool, with no placement and no slot, comes back this way (#473). A clip that
sits in the launch grid is refused: copying or linking it is
`arrangement.place_from_slot` (founder's decision 11). `start` is in
ticks; `offset` (default 0, before the clip's length) is where in the clip the
placement starts; `length` (default: what is left of the clip after `offset`) is
its length on the timeline, which may exceed the clip (the clip repeats: its loop
when it has one, the whole clip when it has none). The new placement wins on overlap: the
other placements of the track that it covers are removed, shortened, trimmed at
the front or split (`overwritten` counts them). An audio clip of an audio track is
placed whole (from its first frame, its end computed from its frames at the project's
tempo, so `length` and `offset` are refused); there the new placement never carves:
an overlap, or a span outside `[0, 2^40]` ticks, is refused. Undo: `arrangement.restore`.

Move placements in time, all by the same number of ticks (`by`, negative moves
them earlier), in one command: a drag of a selection is one history entry. Each
placement stays in its own track and keeps its length and offset. The moved
placements win on overlap (the placements of the track that they cover are
carved, `overwritten` counts them); they may move onto each other's old place.
Refused when one would start before tick 0 or end past 2^40, or when the list is
empty, names a placement twice or an unknown one. A move by 0 changes nothing.
Undo: `arrangement.restore`.

Move placements to other MIDI tracks, in one command and one history entry, and
optionally in time too (`by` ticks, default 0, negative is earlier). `moves` pairs
each placement with the track it ends in (its own track keeps it there): a selection
of several tracks can move one track down together, each clip to its own target.
The clip of a moved placement goes with it: the target track gets a copy of the
clip (one copy per source clip and target track, so placements that were linked and
move together stay linked; same name, colour, length, loop and notes, not in the
launch grid), and a source clip left with no placement and no grid slot is removed
from its track (a clip in the grid, or one still placed elsewhere, stays). The
moved placements get new identifiers in another track (`placements`, in the order of
`moves`) and keep their length and offset; they win on overlap in the target (the
placements they cover are carved, `overwritten` counts them). Refused when `moves`
is empty, names a placement twice or an unknown one, names an unknown track or one
that is not a MIDI track (audio clips come from import), when a placement is an
audio one, when one would start before tick 0 or end past 2^40, or on a limit.
Nothing moves (and no history entry is made) when every placement stays in its
track and `by` is 0. Undo: `arrangement.restore`, which puts the placements and the
removed clips back with their identifiers and removes the copies.

Move one edge of a placement to the timeline tick `to`. `edge: "end"` changes the
length (the end must stay after the start); `edge: "start"` moves the start with
the end fixed, and the offset follows so the content does not slide: shortening
from the left cuts the beginning of the clip (through the clip's loop), growing to
the left shows earlier content and is refused beyond the clip's start (offset 0).
The resized placement wins on overlap (the others it now covers are carved,
`overwritten` counts them). Moving the edge where it is changes nothing. Undo:
`arrangement.restore`.

Split a placement in two at the timeline tick `at`, strictly inside it: the left
part keeps the identifier, the right part is a new placement (the same clip, so
linked) that plays on from where the left one stops (round the clip's loop, or round
the whole clip when it has none). Undo:
`arrangement.restore`.

Delete placements, in one command, MIDI or audio ones. Their clips stay in their
tracks, even one that loses its last placement and sits in no grid slot: it stays in
the track's pool (an audio clip keeps its file; `arrangement.place` puts a clip back,
MIDI or audio; `clip.delete` deletes a clip). Refused when the
list is empty, names a placement twice or an unknown one. Undo:
`arrangement.restore`.

Copy placements, in one command. The copies start `by` ticks after the originals
(default: right after the selection, one selection length later; negative copies
earlier). By default each copy is independent: a new clip, a copy of the source
(same name, colour, length, loop and notes; not
in the launch grid), one per
distinct source clip, so placements that were linked stay linked among the copies
and editing a copy never changes the original (founder's decision 11). With
`linked: true` the copies are new placements of the same clips. The copies win
on overlap (`overwritten` counts the placements they carved). Refused when the
list is empty, names a placement twice or an unknown one, or when a copy would
leave the timeline. Undo: `arrangement.restore`, which removes the copies and
the clips created.

Repeat one placement end to end up to the timeline tick `until` (#555): linked
copies, new placements of the same clip, each as long as the placement and with
its offset, the first starting where the placement ends, the next where the last
ends; the one that would pass `until` is shortened to stop exactly there. To fill
up to the end of bar N, give the tick where bar N ends. The copies win on overlap
(`overwritten` counts the placements they carved). Refused when the placement is
unknown or an audio one, when `until` is not after the end of the placement or
passes 2^40, or when the copies would pass the limit of placements. One history
entry; undo: `arrangement.restore`, which removes the copies and brings back what
they carved.

Put a MIDI clip of the launch grid in the arrangement, on its own track, as a
placement at the timeline tick `start` that plays the whole clip once (offset 0,
the clip's length). By default the placement plays an independent copy: a new
clip, a copy of the grid clip (same name, colour, length, loop and notes, not in
the launch grid), so editing one never changes the other (founder's decision 11).
With `linked: true` the placement references the grid clip itself: editing the
clip in the grid changes what the arrangement plays. The placement wins on overlap
(`overwritten` counts the placements it carved). Refused for a clip that is not in
the launch grid (use `arrangement.place` or `arrangement.duplicate`), for an audio
clip, or when the clip would leave the timeline. Undo: `arrangement.restore`,
which removes the placement and the copy.

`arrangement.place_from_slot` for a whole scene of the launch grid, in one command
and one history entry: every MIDI clip of the scene is placed on its own track at
the same tick `start`, as a copy (default) or linked to the grid clip. Empty slots
place nothing; audio clips are skipped. Refused when the scene has no MIDI clip.
The placements win on overlap. Undo: `arrangement.restore`.

Insert `length` ticks of empty time at the timeline tick `at`, in every track and in
the master, in one history entry (bar-level editing: a bar is 3840 ticks in 4/4).
A placement that starts at or after `at` moves `length` ticks later; one that
straddles `at` is split there, the right part (a new placement of the same clip, so
linked) moving later and resuming the clip where the left part stops, round the clip.
The points of every automation lane at or after `at` move too (a ramp that straddles
`at` stretches), so do the section markers at or after `at` (#473), and so do the
loop region's boundaries after `at` (a loop that contains `at` grows). Tempo and time
signature hold one point at tick 0 and do not move; the playhead and the launch grid
do not move. Refused with `invalid` when `at` is not in [0, 2^40], `length` is less
than 1 or the cut would pass 2^40, or when a placement or a point would pass 2^40,
and with `limit` when the splits pass the placement limits. Refused too, for the
whole project, while any track holds an audio placement (`clip.import_audio` into
the arrangement makes one): audio placements do not move in time yet. Changes nothing
(no history entry) when nothing lies at or after `at`. Undo: `arrangement.restore_time`.

Delete the time `[from, to)` ticks from every track and from the master,
and close the gap, in one history entry. Placements are cut at both edges: what lies
inside is removed (a placement that straddles the whole range is split in two, the
right part a new placement resuming the clip where the range ends), what starts at or
after `to` moves `to - from` ticks earlier; a clip that loses its last placement stays
in its track's pool. The points of every automation lane inside the range are removed and the
later ones move back, so the last point before the cut links straight to the first
one after it (a `step` point keeps holding its value up to the cut, then the next
value applies: the lane is not smoothed). The section markers after the range move
back, one inside it goes to `from` (#473). The loop region follows (a boundary inside
the range falls to `from`;
a loop left empty is cleared and switched off). Tempo and time signature hold one
point at tick 0 and do not move; the playhead and the launch grid do not move.
Refused with `invalid` when `from` is not in [0, 2^40], `to` is not after `from` or
passes 2^40, and with `limit` when the cuts pass the placement limits. Refused too, for
the whole project, while any track holds an audio placement (audio placements do not
move in time yet). Changes nothing (no history entry) when nothing lies at or after
`from`. Undo:
`arrangement.restore_time`.

The inverse of `arrangement.insert_time` and `arrangement.delete_time`: write the
placements as `arrangement.restore` does (`edits`, may be empty here), replace the
points of the named automation lanes by exactly those given (`lanes`, a value kept as
it is, within the parameter's range), put the loop settings back (`transport`,
absent: untouched) and the section markers at their ticks (`markers`), in one history
entry and all or nothing. Refused when nothing is given, when a lane or a marker is
unknown or listed twice, when a point or a marker is out of range, when the loop is
on without a region, or for any reason `arrangement.restore` refuses.
Undo: the restore of what it changed.

markers.description: The section markers to put back at their ticks (#473).

oneOf.description:
Write the placements of one or more tracks exactly as given, without the overlap
rule: the inverse of every arrangement command, which brings back what it carved,
with the identifiers. Per track: `put` creates or replaces placements by
identifier, `remove` removes placements, `clips` brings back MIDI clips (new
identifiers, a snapshot as `clip.restore` takes) and `remove_clips` removes clips.
Refused when a placement is outside the timeline or its offset outside its clip,
when a placement is left on a removed clip or names an unknown clip, when an
identifier to create is in use, or when a rule of the clip commands is broken (a
note outside the length, a limit). In an audio track only `put` and `remove` of
audio placements (a record with `frames`) are taken, never `clips` or `remove_clips`.
Undo: the restore of what it changed.

Add a named section marker (a named point of the arrangement, not the transport's
cue) at the timeline tick `tick` (960 per quarter note, 0 to
2^40). `name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters): left out, empty or only
spaces, the marker is called "Section n", n the first number no marker has (a blank
name means "no name", unlike `arrangement.marker.rename`, which refuses it because it
has no default to fall back on). Refused with `limit` past 1 024 markers. Undo: `arrangement.marker.delete`.

Rename a marker. The name is trimmed, not empty, at most 200 characters. Undo:
rename it back.
Move a marker to the timeline tick `tick` (0 to 2^40). Undo: move it back.

Delete a marker. Not destructive: undo (`arrangement.marker.restore`) brings it back with its
identifier.

Bring back a deleted marker with its identifier: the inverse of `arrangement.marker.delete`.
Refused when the identifier is already in use in the project, or for a tick or a name
`arrangement.marker.add` would refuse. Undo: `arrangement.marker.delete`.

List the section markers of the arrangement in timeline order (tick, then
identifier): each with its identifier, its tick (960 per quarter note) and its name.
A query: changes nothing and never enters the history.

oneOf.description:
Create an empty automation lane on a parameter of a track or of the master. Name the
owner with `track` (a track's identifier) or with `master: true` (the master),
exactly one of the two. `target` is
`{"device": {"device": <device id>, "param": <parameter key>}}` for a parameter of
one of the owner's devices (the keys are in the device descriptors of the schema
bundle; the device must be in the owner's chain: a track's, or the master's effects)
or `{"mixer": {"param": "gain"}}` / `{"mixer": {"param": "pan"}}` for the owner's
volume or pan (there is no mute lane). Refused with `not_found` for an unknown track,
for a device that is not in the owner's chain (another track's, or the master's for a
track's lane) or a parameter the device lacks, with `invalid` when both or neither of
`track` and `master` are given or when the owner already has a lane on that parameter,
and with `limit` at the safety limit of lanes.
A new lane has no point yet and has no effect on the sound until points are added
with `automation.points.add`: create the lane, then add its points. Once it has points,
it holds the first point's value from the start of the timeline until that point, and the engine applies
its value at the playhead when the transport stops and at every seek, so a lane with a
single point at bar 9 already sets its parameter from bar 1. A lane belongs to the
track, not to its clips. Undo: `automation.lane.delete`.

master.description: `true` for a lane of the master instead of a track's.

track.description: The track that owns the lane; absent for the master.

oneOf.description:
Delete an automation lane with all its points. Undo: `automation.lane.restore`
brings it back with its identifier and points.

Bring a deleted lane back under its identifier, as `automation.lane.delete` took it
out: the inverse of a delete. `track` or `master: true` names the owner, as for
`automation.lane.create`. `snapshot` is the whole lane: its target and points.
Refused when the identifier is already in use, when both or neither of `track` and
`master` are given, when the track does not exist, when the target is not valid for
the owner, at the safety limit of lanes, or when a point is not valid. Undo:
`automation.lane.delete`.

master.description: `true` for a lane of the master instead of a track's.

track.description: The track that owns the lane; absent for the master.

oneOf.description:
Add points to a lane, in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing). Each point
is `{tick, value, shape}`: `tick` 0 to 2^40, `value` in the parameter's unit (rounded
to its step; a device parameter is clamped to its range, a gain outside -96..+6 dB or
a pan outside -1..1 is refused), `shape` `linear` (default) or `step`; a linear segment
of a volume lane is a straight line along the fader's travel (not in amplitude nor in
dB), of any other lane a straight line in its unit. A lane has at
most one point per tick: a tick that already holds a different point, or that appears
twice in the batch, is refused (use `automation.points.update` to change a point); a
point equal to the one already there changes nothing. Refused with `limit` past the
safety limit of points per lane or in the project. Before its first point a lane holds
the first point's value (from tick 0, bar 1), so the first point sets the value of
everything before it: to keep a parameter at its current value until a change, add a
point at tick 0 with that value. Points are at absolute ticks of the timeline, they do
not follow clips. Undo: `automation.points.remove` of the points actually added.

Remove the points at these ticks from a lane, in one batch (one history entry). A
tick that holds no point is ignored; the output counts the points removed. Undo:
`automation.points.restore` puts the points actually removed back, exactly as they were.

Change the value or the shape of points of a lane, in one batch (one history entry,
all or nothing). Each point names the tick of an existing point and gives its new
`value` (the same rules as `automation.points.add`) and `shape`; the position does
not change (remove and add to move a point). Refused with `not_found` when a tick
holds no point and with `invalid` when a tick appears twice. A point that ends equal
changes nothing. Undo: `automation.points.restore` puts the previous points back,
exactly as they were.

Remove all the points of a lane and keep the lane. Undo: `automation.points.restore`
puts the points back, exactly as they were.

Put points back in a lane exactly as given, and take the points at `remove` out: the
inverse of `automation.points.remove`, `automation.points.update` and
`automation.lane.clear`, one history entry, all or nothing. Unlike
`automation.points.add`, a value is kept as it is (not rounded to the step), so that an
undo gives back the very points that were there; a point at a tick that already holds
one replaces it. A tick in range, a finite value within the parameter's range (a
device parameter's, -96 to +6 dB for a gain, -1 to 1 for a pan) are still required, and
the safety limits of points. Refused when
a tick is in both lists or twice in one. Undo: `automation.points.restore` with the
points it replaced and the ticks it added.

remove.description: The ticks whose points are taken out; absent: none.

oneOf.description:
List automation lanes, without their points (`automation.lane.points` reads them):
each with its identifier, its owner track (`null` for the master's), its target
(a device parameter or the owner's `gain` or `pan`) and how many points it holds.
Name `track` for one track's lanes or `master: true` for the master's, not both
(refused with `invalid`); with neither, every lane of the project: the master's
first, then each track's in display order, a track's lanes in the order of their
identifiers. Refused with `not_found` for an unknown track. Paged: `offset` (lanes to
skip, 0 by default) and `limit` (lanes to return, 1 to 1000, 100 by default; any
other limit is refused with `invalid`, never clamped); the answer's `page` gives the
`total`, the `offset` used and the `next_offset` of the next page, `null` after the
last one. A query: changes nothing and never enters the history.

limit.description: Lanes to return, 1 to 1000, 100 by default.

offset.description: Lanes to skip, 0 by default.

track.description: Only this track's lanes.

oneOf.description:
Read the points of one automation lane in tick order, a page at a time: each point
has its `tick` (0 to 2^40, 960 per quarter note), its `value` in the parameter's unit
(dB for a gain lane) and its `shape` (`linear` or `step`, the transition to the next
point). The answer also gives the lane's summary (owner, target, point count). Paged:
`offset` (points to skip, 0 by default) and `limit` (points to return, 1 to 1000, 100
by default; any other limit is refused with `invalid`, never clamped); the answer's
`page` gives the `total`, the `offset` used and the `next_offset` of the next page,
`null` after the last one. An `offset` past the end gives an empty page. Refused with
`not_found` for an unknown lane. A query: changes nothing and never enters the
history.

lane.description: The lane whose points are read.

limit.description: Points to return, 1 to 1000, 100 by default.

offset.description: Points to skip, 0 by default.

AutomationLane.description: A parameter's curve over time, in a track's arrangement.

points.description: Points by tick: at most one point per tick.

AutomationPoint.description: A value at a tick and the shape of the transition to the next point.

oneOf.description: A parameter of a device of the same track.
A parameter of the track's mixer.

Clip.description:
A clip: the content. A slot puts it in the launch grid, a [`Placement`] in the
arrangement. Copying a clip makes a new, independent clip (founder's decision 11); two
placements of the same clip are linked clips.

launch_quantize.description:
Reserved for a per-clip launch quantization after the MVP: absent means the
project setting. The MVP never writes it.

slot.description: The scene of the launch-grid slot the clip sits in.

ClipCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Create an empty MIDI clip in a MIDI track, in the launch grid (`{"at": "slot",
"scene": <scene id>}`: the slot must exist and be free) or in the arrangement
(`{"at": "arrangement", "start": <tick>}`: also places the whole clip there, and
is refused when it would overlap another placement of the track). `length` is in
ticks (960 per quarter note), one bar of the project's time signature by default.
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters): without one the clip gets the
next default name of its track, the track's name and the first number no clip of
the track has with it ("Bass 3"); it is stored and never changes when other clips
move, are copied or deleted, nor when the track is renamed. Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Delete a clip (MIDI or audio) and its placements in the arrangement. Undo:
`clip.restore` brings back a MIDI clip, its notes and its placements with their
identifiers; `clip.restore_audio` an audio clip and its placements. The file of an
audio clip stays in the project's `blobs/` (blobs are removed on request only).

Bring back a MIDI clip with its identifier, as `clip.delete` removed it: the
inverse of a delete. Refused when the track is not a MIDI track, when the clip's
identifier or a placement's already exists in the project, when the slot is
taken or its scene is gone, or when the snapshot breaks a rule of the clip
commands (a note outside the length, a placement outside the timeline). Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Make an audio clip in an audio track from an imported audio file (AU-1). `media` is
the SHA-256 of the file (64 lower-case hexadecimal characters, the name of its blob):
either a file the page has just imported (the page reads the file the user chose,
stores its bytes in the project's `blobs/` and stages its metadata before running
this command), or a file an audio clip of the project already uses (`clip.get` shows
its `media.hash`), so another clip of the same file needs no new import. The clip
plays the whole file, at 0 dB, without a loop. `at` is optional: without it (or
`null`) the clip sits in the track's pool (no launch-grid slot, no placement); with
`{"at": "slot", "scene": <scene id>}` it sits in that launch-grid slot (the scene must
exist and the slot be free in the track); with `{"at": "arrangement", "start": <tick>}`
it is also placed whole in the arrangement from that tick (its end is computed from
the file's duration at the project's tempo), refused when that placement would
overlap another placement of the track or end past 2^40. `name` is optional (trimmed,
at most 200 characters): without one the clip takes the file's name without its
extension. Refused when the track is not an audio track or the media is unknown.
Undo: `clip.delete` of the clip (and of its placement); the file stays in the
project's `blobs/` (blobs are removed on request only).

Set the range of the file an audio clip plays: the frames `[start, start + frames)`
of its file (frames of the file, at its own sample rate). Refused when the range is
empty or leaves the file, when the clip's loop would end past the new length (clear
or move the loop first with `clip.audio.set_loop`: nothing is cut silently), and when
a placement of the clip starts inside it at or past the new length. Every placement
that plays the clip whole (offset 0, length equal to its old length in frames) takes
the new length in the same command; a growing placement stops at the start of the
next placement of its track; a placement that plays only part of the clip is left
alone. Refused for a MIDI clip. Undo: set the range back, with the lengths of the
placements.

frames.description: How many frames are played, at least 1.

start.description: First frame of the file played.

oneOf.description:
Set an audio clip's gain in dB, from -96 to +6; `null` is silence. A value outside
the range or not a number is refused, and so is a MIDI clip. Undo: set the previous
gain back.

gain_db.description: Required: `null` is silence, a missing field is an error.

oneOf.description:
Set an audio clip's loop: `{"start": <frame>, "end": <frame>}` in frames from the
clip's start (not from the file's), with `0 <= start < end <= frames` (the clip's
length in frames), or `null` for no loop. Refused for a MIDI clip (`clip.set_loop`
sets its loop in ticks). Undo: set the previous loop back.

Bring back an audio clip with its identifier, as `clip.delete` removed it: the
inverse of deleting an audio clip. Its placements give their length and offset in
frames of the file. Refused when the track is not an audio track, when the clip's
identifier or a placement's already exists in the project, when the slot is taken
or its scene is gone, or when the snapshot breaks a rule of the project (a range
outside the file, a loop outside the range, a gain that is not a number). Undo:
`clip.delete`.

Ask the user for audio files to import into an audio track (AU-1): the page opens
its file dialog, then imports each file chosen (its bytes are kept in the project's
`blobs/`, its decoded audio checked) and makes a clip of it with `clip.import_audio`.
A file dialog needs a click by the user, so an agent that is not driven by one gets a
notice in the page instead. Formats: WAV, AIFF, CAF, FLAC, MP3, AAC (MP4, M4A, ADTS),
ALAC, Ogg Vorbis; Opus is not supported yet. The answer only says the request was
accepted; the clips arrive with `clip.import_audio`, one history entry each. Refused
when the track is not an audio track. Not undoable itself.

Stop the audio import under way in the page (the files chosen by `clip.choose_audio`):
the file being imported is dropped (nothing of it is kept) and the files after it are
not imported; the clips of the files already imported stay. Does nothing when no import
runs. Not undoable itself.

Copy a MIDI clip into a new, independent clip with the same name ("Bass 2" stays
"Bass 2": a copy plays the same part), colour, length, loop and notes; editing one never changes the other. The copy always sits in a
launch-grid slot: of the source's track, or of `track` when given (another MIDI
track). `slot` when given must be free in that track, otherwise the copy takes
the first free slot (below the source's scene in the same track, from the top in
another). Refused, with no effect, when the track has no free slot to give. A
second placement of the same clip is an option of the arrangement commands, not
of this one. Undo: `clip.delete` of the copy.

Move a clip to another launch-grid slot, of the same track or of `track` (another
track of its kind: a MIDI clip to a MIDI track, an audio clip to an audio track),
keeping its identifier, its name and its content. `slot`
is the scene of the target slot, which must be free; `null` takes the clip out of
the grid (with no placement, it stays in its track's pool, #473). A clip
that has placements stays in its track: moving it to another track is refused.
A move that changes nothing does nothing and leaves no history entry. Leaving
`slot` out is the same as `null`. The engine frees the clip and takes it again, so
a clip that is playing stops, and so does the arrangement's playback of its
placements (they play again from the next note). Undo: move it back.

Rename a clip (MIDI or audio). The name is trimmed, at most 200 characters; an
empty name gives a MIDI clip the next default name of its track ("Bass 3"; one that
already has a default name of its track keeps it) and clears an audio clip's. Undo: rename it back.

Set the length of a MIDI clip, in ticks (1 to 2^40). Making it shorter than a
note's end or the loop's end is refused, unless `trim` is true: then notes that
start at or after the new end are removed, notes that cross it are shortened
(two notes that become identical merge into one), and the loop is cut at it
(removed when nothing is left of it). Refused too when a placement of the clip
starts inside it past the new length. Every placement of the clip that plays it
whole (offset 0, length equal to the old length of the clip) takes the new length
in the same command, so notes added past the old end are heard in the
arrangement; a growing placement stops at the start of the next placement of its
track, and a placement that shows only part of the clip, or repeats it, is left
alone. Undo: set the length back, restoring what `trim` cut and the lengths of the
placements.

Set the loop of a MIDI clip: `{"start": <tick>, "end": <tick>}` with
`0 <= start < end <= length`, or `null` for no loop. Undo: set the previous loop
back.

Replace the length, the loop and all the notes of a MIDI clip at once: one
history entry for a whole clip written in one go. The same rules as
`clip.set_length`, `clip.set_loop` and `clip.notes.add` apply (a note outside
`[0, length]` is refused), and the placements follow the length in the same way
as `clip.set_length`. Undo: set the previous content and the previous placement
lengths back.

Add notes to a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing).
A note has `start` and `length` in ticks (the note must lie inside
`[0, clip length]`, length at least 1), `pitch` 0 to 127, `velocity` 1 to 127,
and optionally `cents` (fine tuning, -50 to 50), `chance` (0 to 100 percent,
default 100) and `repeat` (1 to 16, default 1). A note outside the clip is
refused, never truncated. A note already in the clip changes nothing. Undo:
remove the notes actually added.

Remove notes from a MIDI clip, in one batch (one history entry), each addressed
by its whole value (start, pitch, length, velocity and the optional fields). A
note that is not in the clip is ignored; the output counts those removed. Undo:
add the notes actually removed.

Change notes of a MIDI clip in one batch (one history entry, all or nothing):
position, length, pitch, velocity, cents, chance or repeat. Each change gives
the note as it is now (`from`) and as it becomes (`to`, the same rules as
`clip.notes.add`). All the `from` notes leave and all the `to` notes arrive at
once, so a chain or a swap is fine. Refused when a `from` is not in the clip,
when two changes share a `from` or a `to`, or when a `to` equals a note that
stays. A change that ends with the same notes changes nothing. Undo: the
opposite changes.

Quantize the start of notes of a MIDI clip toward a grid, in one batch (one history
entry, all or nothing). `grid` is the grid step in ticks (960 per quarter note, at
least 1); `strength` is 0 to 100 percent: 100 puts a note on the nearest grid line
(halfway goes to the later line), 50 moves it half of the way, 0 changes nothing.
`notes` lists the notes to quantize, each by its whole value; leave it out to
quantize every note of the clip. A listed note that is not in the clip is refused.
Only the start moves: the length never changes. A note that the move would push past
the end of the clip stops where it still fits (its end on the clip's end), so it may
be off the grid. Notes that end up equal merge into one. Undo: the opposite moves
(the previous content of the clip when notes merged).

Transpose notes of a MIDI clip by `semitones` (positive up, negative down), in one
batch (one history entry, all or nothing). Each note is addressed by its whole
value and must be in the clip. A transposition that would take one note outside
pitch 0 to 127 is refused for the whole batch, never clamped. Notes that end up
equal merge into one. 0 semitones changes nothing. Undo: transpose back (the
previous content of the clip when notes merged).

Copy notes of a MIDI clip, shifted in time by `offset` ticks (negative: earlier), in
one batch (one history entry, all or nothing). Each source note is addressed by its
whole value and must be in the clip. Without `offset`, the copies follow the whole
selection: the shift is the span from the start of the bar of the first note to the last
end, rounded up to whole bars (at least one bar), so a selection of one bar or less is
copied to the next bar and a selection of two bars two bars later. An `offset` of 0
is refused, and so is a copy that would lie outside `[0, clip length]` (never
truncated). A copy equal to a note already in the clip changes nothing. Undo: remove
the notes actually added.

Read one clip, MIDI or audio, without its notes (`clip.notes.list` pages them): the
track that holds it, its summary (name, colour, launch-grid slot, kind, length and
note count of a MIDI clip), its own launch quantization when it has one, its content
(a MIDI clip's length in ticks, loop and note count; an audio clip's media, range of
frames, gain in dB with `null` for silence, and loop) and a page of its placements
in the track's arrangement, in the order of their identifiers. Paged on the
placements: `offset` (placements to skip, 0 by default) and `limit` (placements to
return, 1 to 1000, 100 by default; any other limit is refused with `invalid`, never
clamped); the answer's `page` gives the `total`, the `offset` used and the
`next_offset` of the next page, `null` after the last one. Refused with `not_found`
for an unknown clip. A query: changes nothing and never enters the history.

limit.description: Placements to return, 1 to 1000, 100 by default.

offset.description: Placements to skip, 0 by default.

oneOf.description:
List the notes of a MIDI clip in time order (start, then pitch, then length, then
the other fields of the note): each note has `start` and `length` in ticks (960 per
quarter note, from the start of the clip), `pitch` (MIDI key 0 to 127) and
`velocity` (1 to 127), and its `cents`, `chance` and `repeat` when they are not the
default. A note is addressed in the edit commands by this whole value. Paged: `offset`
(notes to skip, 0 by default) and `limit` (notes to return, 1 to 1000, 100 by
default; any other limit is refused with `invalid`, never clamped); the answer's
`page` gives the `total`, the `offset` used and the `next_offset` of the next page,
`null` after the last one. An `offset` past the end gives an empty page. Refused with
`not_found` for an unknown clip and with `invalid` for an audio clip, which has no
notes. A query: changes nothing and never enters the history.

clip.description: The MIDI clip whose notes are listed.

limit.description: Notes to return, 1 to 1000, 100 by default.

offset.description: Notes to skip, 0 by default.

oneOf.description: Musical time: length and loop in ticks.

Source time: a range `[start, start + frames)` of an audio file, in frames. No
length in ticks is stored: it is computed at the project's tempo.

gain_db.description: Clip gain in dB; `-inf` is written `null`.

ClipRecord.description: A MIDI clip that `arrangement.restore` brings back, with its identifier.

state.description: What the clip becomes; `null` removes it with its placements.

ClipSnapshot.description: A MIDI clip as `clip.restore` brings it back (everything but its identifier).

launch_quantize.description: A per-clip launch quantization, when one was set (the MVP never sets one).

slot.description: The scene of its launch-grid slot, when it sits in one.

oneOf.description: In the launch grid, at the intersection of the track and a scene.
In the arrangement: a placement of the whole clip from `start` (in ticks).

Device.description:
A link of a track's chain. Its display name is its type's single English name, never
translated nor stored here.

params.description: Parameter id → value in the unit the device declares.

preset.description:
The preset the device was last set from (#191), by `preset.load` or `preset.save`;
absent when none, so that a device without one writes the same file as before.

state.description: Opaque instrument state, stored as a blob.

DeviceCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Insert an effect in a track's chain, or in the master's. Name the chain with
`track` (a track's identifier) or with `master: true` (the master: the effects
there process the sum of all the tracks before the master's volume), exactly one
of the two. `kind` is the type id of a built-in effect (an instrument is refused:
`track.set_instrument` replaces a track's instrument, and the master has none).
`index` is the position among the chain's effects, 0 first (right after the
instrument on a track); an index past the end means last. The new device starts at
its default settings, not bypassed. Refused with `invalid` when both or neither of
`track` and `master` are given, when the effects around that position share an
order key (a merge made them equal), and with `limit` at the safety limit of
devices per chain. Undo: `device.remove`.

master.description: `true` to insert in the master's chain instead of a track's.

track.description: The track whose chain gets the effect; absent for the master.

oneOf.description:
Remove an effect from its track or from the master, with its settings. The
automation lanes that target the effect are deleted with it. Refused for an
instrument (the oscillator, the clip player: replace it with `track.set_instrument`).
Undo: `device.restore` brings it back with its identifier, position, settings, bypass
and automation lanes.

Bring a removed effect back with its identifier, as `device.remove` took it out:
the inverse of a remove. `track` or `master: true` names the chain, as for
`device.insert`. `snapshot` is the whole device: its order key, bypass, source,
settings and state. Refused when both or neither of `track` and `master` are given,
when the identifier is already in use, at the safety limit of devices, or when the
snapshot is not an effect (a built-in device must be one of the registry, with only
parameters it declares; a module device is taken as it is) or does not fit the
chain. `lanes` are the automation lanes that targeted the device, as `device.remove`
took them out (absent: none); each must target this device and a parameter it has,
under an identifier not in use. Undo: `device.remove`.

lanes.description: The automation lanes of the device, by identifier.

master.description: `true` to restore into the master's chain instead of a track's.

track.description: The track whose chain gets the effect back; absent for the master.

oneOf.description:
Move an effect to `index` among the effects of its chain (a track's or the master's),
0 first (right after the instrument on a track); an index past the end means last. The instrument cannot be moved.
Refused with `invalid` when the effects around that position share an order key.
Undo: `device.restore_order` puts the exact previous order key back.

Put an effect back under an exact order key: the inverse of `device.move`, which
takes an index. Refused when the key would put the effect before the instrument.
Undo: set the key before this command back.

Bypass a device (`bypass: true`: the chain skips it, its settings are kept) or put
it back (`false`). An instrument that is bypassed is silent. Refused for the clip
player of an audio track. Undo: set the previous state back.

Set a parameter of a device, by the parameter's id, in the unit the device
declares. The parameter must be one the device declares and the value must be
finite; it is clamped to the parameter's range and rounded to its step, and the
value stored (and returned) is the result. The built-in synth's parameters:
`waveform` (0 sine, 1 saw, 2 square, 3 triangle), `attack`, `decay` and
`release` (seconds, 0.002 to 30), `sustain` (0 to 1), `gain` (0 to 1, linear).
Every device's parameters (key, unit, range, default, and a `description` of what
each does) are in the device descriptors of the schema bundle. Undo: set the parameter back to its previous value.

Describe a device, or a built-in device kind before any is inserted. Give exactly
one of `device` (the id of a device of a track's chain or of the master's) and
`kind` (a built-in kind such as `faulk.osc_synth`); both or neither is refused with
`invalid`, an unknown device or kind with `not_found`. For a device the answer has its
summary (id, role, bypass state, source, English name), the track that holds it
(`null` for the master's chain) and the current value of every parameter, by
parameter key. For a built-in kind, and for a built-in device, it has the kind's
descriptor: version, English name, role and every parameter's key, `description`,
unit, range, default, scale, step and enumerated `values`, and the named keys of a
drum-like instrument. A module and the clip player have no descriptor (`null`). A
query: changes nothing and never enters the history.

device.description: A device to describe; leave out when giving `kind`.

kind.description: A built-in kind to describe; leave out when giving `device`.

DeviceId.description: Identifier of a device in a track's chain or in the master's.

DevicePreset.description:
The preset a device was last set from, kept on the device so that its panel names it
after a reload and on another computer (where a library preset may be absent).

id.description:
The preset's id in its location: a factory id (`faulk.osc_synth/round-bass`) or a
ULID.

name.description: The preset's name when the device was set from it.

DeviceRestore.description: The preset a device shows, as `preset.restore` puts it back.

preset.description: The preset the device shows; absent or `null` for none.

DeviceRole.description: What a device does in the chain.

DeviceSource.description: Where a device comes from. Third-party plugins come after the MVP.

oneOf.description: A device built into Faulk, by type id (`"faulk.osc_synth"`) and version.
A module of the Workshop, by name and the hash of its compiled code.

Edge.description: The edge of a placement that `arrangement.resize` moves.

oneOf.description:
The left edge: the end stays where it is, the placement shows the clip from
further on (or earlier).
The right edge: the start and the offset stay.
16-bit integers.
24-bit integers.

32-bit floats. The output protection (#402) holds every format, floats included, under
−0.3 dBFS, so no format clips; the choice is only size and precision, not headroom.

ExportRegion.description: Which part of the project is rendered.

oneOf.description: From the start to the end of the last placement of the arrangement, then the tail.

From the start of bar `from_bar` to the end of bar `to_bar` (both counted from 1, the
