FrameLoop.description:
An audio clip's loop `[start, end)` in source frames, relative to the clip's start,
within `[0, frames]`.

FrameSpan.description: The span of an audio placement, in frames of the clip's file.

length.description: How many frames of the clip the placement plays, at least 1.

offset.description: The frame of the clip where it starts, before the clip's frame count.

Hash.description: The SHA-256 of a blob, 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters.

HistoryCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Undo the last entry of the history: one command, or every command of one
history group. Does nothing when there is nothing to undo; refused while a
group is open. Undo: `history.redo`.

Open a history group: every edit of the same author until `history.end_group`
becomes one entry, undone at once (a mouse drag). Refused when a group is
already open (groups do not nest). Undo and redo are refused while it is open:
the host ends it when the gesture or the turn ends. Not undoable itself.

Close the open history group. Refused when no group is open, or when another
author opened it. Not undoable itself.

Id.description: A stable identifier: 26 characters of Crockford base32 (a ULID), generated by the project.

InputGrid.description:
The grids a take can be quantized to on input: the ones of the piano roll's quantize
field (`clip.notes.quantize`), plus none.

oneOf.description: The notes stay as played.

LanePoints.description: The points of one automation lane, written whole by `arrangement.restore_time`.

lane.description: A lane of a track or of the master.

points.description: All the points the lane holds afterwards, at most one per tick.

LaunchCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Launch a clip of the launch grid, MIDI or audio, at the next boundary of the launch
quantization; it replaces the clip its track plays. The clip must sit in a slot of
the grid (a clip of the arrangement only cannot be launched). An audio clip plays
from its first frame at the boundary, at its gain, looped when it has a loop, else
once to its last frame. If the transport is stopped, it starts playing from its
position, so the clip starts at the first boundary. Played live: not undoable, not
saved.

Launch every clip of a scene at the same boundary: each track plays the clip of its
slot in the scene, and a track whose slot is empty stops. An empty scene stops every
track that plays. If the transport is stopped, it starts playing from its position.
Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Stop the clip a track plays, or cancel the launch it waits for, at the next boundary
of the launch quantization. Does not start the transport. Played live: not undoable,
not saved.

Stop every track that plays a clip or waits for a launch, at the next boundary of
the launch quantization; it replaces the launches waiting. Does not start the
transport, and does not stop it. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Give every track back to its arrangement: a clip launched from the grid (or a stop
given from it) takes a track until this command. The notes of the grid's clips end
at once, launches still waiting for their boundary are dropped, and each track plays
its arrangement again from the playhead (a note already started on the timeline is
not restarted: it stays silent until its end). Does nothing to a track that follows
its arrangement. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Give one track back to its arrangement: what `launch.back_to_arrangement` does, for
the track alone; the other tracks are left as they are. Does nothing to a track that
follows its arrangement. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

LiveCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Start a note on a track's instrument. `note` is a MIDI note number, 0 to 127
(60 = middle C); `velocity` 1 to 127, 0 acts as a note off. Played live: not
undoable, not saved.

Release a note started with `live.note_on` on the same track. Played live: not
undoable, not saved.

Play a note on the live input: it goes to the selected track and to every armed
MIDI track, as the session stands now (`view.select_track`, `track.arm`). `note`
is a MIDI note number, 0 to 127 (60 = middle C); `velocity` 1 to 127, 0 acts as a
note off. Release it with `live.input_note_off`, which reaches the same tracks
whatever was selected or armed meanwhile. The output lists the tracks it went to.
`frame` (optional) is when the key was played, as a frame of the host's audio clock
(in the web page, the frame of its audio context; a host without such a clock counts
the engine's samples): a recording places the note at that frame. Without it, or
with a frame more than a second away from the engine's, the note counts from when
the engine takes it. It never delays the sound. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Release a note started with `live.input_note_on`: on the tracks that note went
to, even if the selection or the arming changed since. `frame` (optional) is when
the key was released, as for `live.input_note_on`. Played live: not undoable, not
saved.

A control change (CC) on the live input, channels merged: `controller` 0 to 127,
`value` 0 to 127. It changes no sound by itself: it is reported to the interface
as a `control_change` event, for the automation (AM-5) to take. Controllers 120
(all sound off) and 123 (all notes off) are not sent here: hosts turn them into
`live.all_notes_off`. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Release every playing note on every track (panic button). Not undoable: it
changes no project data.

Cut every sound at once, on every track and the master: the output fades out in about
5 ms, then every instrument's voices (long releases included) and every effect's
tail (echo repeats, reverb) are cleared, without a click. The transport is not
touched. Use it when a sound rings on or feeds back out of control. Not undoable: it
changes no project data.

LoopState.description: The loop settings as `arrangement.restore_time` writes them.

loop_enabled.description: Whether the transport loops; only with a region.

MarkerId.description: Identifier of a section marker of the arrangement (#473).

MarkerTick.description: A section marker at a tick: what `arrangement.restore_time` puts back.

MidiCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
List the MIDI inputs available to the engine. The host answers with its
`midi.inputs` message: the inputs and the one selected.

Choose the MIDI input that plays the selected track. `id` is an id from
`midi.inputs`; `null` disconnects MIDI input. Session state: not undoable, not
saved with the project.

Mixer.description:
Gain, pan and mute of a track or of the master. Solo is not here: it is session state
(founder's decision 10). Sends come after the MVP.

gain_db.description: Gain in dB; `-inf` (silence) is written `null`.

MixerCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Set a track's volume in dB, from -96 to +6; `null` is silence. A value outside
the range or not a number is refused. A fader gesture sent in one history group
is undone in one step. Undo: set the previous volume back.

gain_db.description: Required: `null` is silence, a missing field is an error.

oneOf.description:
Set a track's pan, from -1 (left) to 1 (right). A value outside the range or
not a number is refused. A pan gesture sent in one history group is undone in
one step. Undo: set the previous pan back.

Mute or unmute a track. Mute is saved with the project and versioned. Undo: set
the previous state back.

Set the master's volume in dB, from -96 to +6; `null` is silence. A value
outside the range or not a number is refused. Undo: set the previous volume
back.

gain_db.description: Required: `null` is silence, a missing field is an error.

oneOf.description:
Set the master's pan, from -1 (left) to 1 (right). A value outside the range or
not a number is refused. A pan gesture sent in one history group is undone in one
step. Undo: set the previous pan back.

Solo or unsolo a track. The soloed tracks are those in the session's solo set;
the audio engine applies it from MX-1 on (cumulative: several tracks can be soloed).
Session state: saved with the session, never in the project's files; undoable like
a mute (#473). Undo: set the previous state back.

Read how loud the project sounds now, per track and for the master, from the
meters of the playing engine: how an agent without ears learns whether a song
sounds. Call it while the transport plays (`transport.play`): the meters keep the
largest peak and the loudest RMS since the previous call (at most the last 10
seconds), so a call right after a passage covers it. That RMS is the loudest of
the engine's short windows (about 30 ms), so it reads higher than the RMS of a
whole passage, which is what `project.analyze_render` gives. Levels are in dBFS (0 is
full scale; the master is measured before the output protection, so it can read
above 0), `null` is silence; a peak is the larger of the two channels, an RMS the
power mean of both. `playing` says whether the transport ran: when it did not (or
the audio is not started, or the engine has stopped reporting), every level is
`null`. Tracks come in display order, after their fader and mute. To measure a
stretch without playing it, use `project.analyze_render`. `silenced_frames` above 0
says the output protection silenced an invalid (non-finite) signal since the engine
started, which the levels cannot show. A query: changes nothing
and never enters the history.

Note.description:
A note: a value without an id (CT-4). Its order compares fields in declaration order:
(start, pitch, length, velocity, cents, chance, repeat).

The last three fields are optional in the file: a default value is not written, and an
absent one reads as the default, so a note has exactly one representation. `chance` and
`repeat` are stored and edited here; the clip player reads them with #192.

cents.description: Fine tuning in cents, -50 to 50 (0 by default).

chance.description: Probability that the note plays, in percent, 0 to 100 (100 by default).

repeat.description: How many times the note repeats, 1 to 16 (1 by default).

start.description: Position from the start of the clip, in ticks.

NoteChange.description: A note to replace by another: `clip.notes.update` addresses a note by its whole value.

from.description: The note as it is in the clip now.

NoteCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

OrderKey.description: A fractional order key: elements sort by it.

Output.description: Where a track's signal goes. Only the master in the MVP; groups and returns later.

Placement.description: A clip set in the arrangement.

PlacementId.description: Identifier of a placement in a track's arrangement.

PlacementRecord.description: A placement of a clip as `arrangement.restore` writes it, with its identifier.

clip.description: A clip of the track: a MIDI clip in a MIDI track, an audio clip in an audio track.

frames.description:
An audio placement's span, in frames of its clip's file: given for a placement of
an audio track and only for those.

length.description:
Length on the timeline, in ticks (a MIDI placement; 0 and ignored when `frames` is
given).

offset.description:
Where in the clip the placement starts, in ticks, before the clip's length (a MIDI
placement; 0 and ignored when `frames` is given).

start.description: Start in the arrangement, in ticks.

PlacementSnapshot.description:
A placement of a MIDI clip, with its identifier, as `clip.restore` brings it back. It
belongs to the clip restored: a snapshot cannot place another clip.

length.description: Length on the timeline, in ticks.

offset.description: Where in the clip the placement starts, in ticks, before the clip's length.

start.description: Start in the arrangement, in ticks.

Point.description: A point of a lane, as the commands take and return it.

shape.description:
The transition from this point to the next: `linear` (default) or `step`. `linear`
is a straight line in the parameter's unit, except for a volume (`gain`) lane, where
it is a straight line along the travel of the mixer's fader, the same law as the
lane's axis (-96 dB, silence, at the bottom, 0 dB at 78 % of the travel, +6 dB at the
top): a fade from 0 dB to -96 dB goes down like a fader pulled at constant speed, and
half way is -21 dB, neither -6 dB (amplitude) nor -48 dB (dB). `step` holds the value.

value.description: The value, in the parameter's unit; rounded to its step.

Preset.description: A preset: the values of a device's parameters under a name.

category.description: A category to group it by (such as `Bass`), at most 64 characters; absent when none.

device.description: The device kind the values are for, such as `faulk.osc_synth`.

name.description: Its name: trimmed, not empty, at most 200 characters.

params.description: Parameter id -> value, in the unit the device declares.

version.description: The version of that device kind the values were made with.

PresetCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Save a device's current settings as a new preset named `name` (trimmed, 1 to 200
characters), with an optional `category` (1 to 64 characters), in the `project` (saved
in the project's folder, it travels with the project) or in the user's `library`
(available in every project). The device then shows this preset, not modified. Only a
built-in device with parameters has presets (not the clip player, not a module).
Refused with `invalid` for the `factory` location (read-only), a name already used by
a preset of that device kind in that location, an empty or too long name or category,
and with `limit` when the location is full (1 024 presets in a project, 4 096 in the
library). Undo: `preset.restore` takes the preset out and gives the device its
previous preset back.

category.description: A category to group it by, such as `Bass`; leave out for none.

oneOf.description:
Load a preset into a device: every parameter of the device takes the preset's value
at once (a parameter the preset has no value for takes its default, a value the device
has no parameter for is ignored, a value out of range is clamped), and the device
shows the preset. One undo takes the whole load back. Refused with `not_found` for an
unknown device or preset, with `invalid` for a preset of another device kind, one made
with a newer version of the device than this Faulk has (the message names both
versions), and a device without presets (the clip player, a module). An older preset
is migrated (`migrated_from`). Undo: `preset.restore_device` puts every previous value
and the previous preset back.

Delete a preset of the project or of the library. A factory preset cannot be deleted
(`invalid`); an unknown one is `not_found`. The devices that show it keep its name.
Undo: `preset.restore` brings it back under the same id.

Rename a preset of the project or of the library (trimmed, 1 to 200 characters). The
devices that show it keep the name they had until it is loaded again. Refused with
`invalid` for a factory preset or a name used by another preset of that device kind in
that location, `not_found` for an unknown one. Undo: `preset.restore` puts the preset
back as it was.

Copy a preset (from any location, factory included) into the `project` or the
`library`, as a new preset with the same values, under its own name or `name` when
given. The devices are left as they are: this is how a preset of a project goes into
the library for every project. Refused like `preset.save` (factory location, a name in
use there, a full location), and with `not_found` for an unknown preset. Undo:
`preset.restore` takes the copy out.

name.description: The copy's name; leave out to keep the preset's.

oneOf.description:
List presets: those of the device kind of `device` (a device's id) or of `kind` (a
built-in kind such as `faulk.filter`), or every preset when both are left out (giving
both is `invalid`). Factory presets come first, then the project's, then the
library's, each by name. Each entry has the preset's reference, name, category, device
kind and version, whether it is read-only (factory) or made with a newer version of
the device (`newer`: it cannot be loaded), and the values a load would give the device.
With `device`, the answer also names the preset the device shows (`current`) and
whether its values differ from that preset's (`modified`; `null` when the device shows
no preset or its preset is not here, such as a library preset of another computer). A
query: changes nothing.

device.description: A device whose presets to list; leave out to give `kind` or to list all.

kind.description: A device kind whose presets to list; leave out to give `device` or to list all.

oneOf.description:
Put a preset of the project or of the library back as it was: `snapshot` is the whole
preset (absent or `null` to take it out), under `preset`'s id. With `device`, that
device shows `device.preset` again. The inverse of `preset.save`, `preset.delete`,
`preset.rename` and `preset.copy`; it does not check names against the other presets
(it puts back exactly what was there). Refused with `invalid` for the factory
location, an id that is not a preset id or that another part of the project uses, a
snapshot that breaks the preset format, and with `limit` when the location is full;
`not_found` for an unknown device. Undo: `preset.restore` with what was there before.

device.description: A device whose shown preset to put back as well.

snapshot.description: The preset to put back; absent or `null` to take it out.

oneOf.description:
Set several parameters of a built-in device at once, by key (each clamped and rounded
as `device.set_param` does), and the preset the device shows (`preset`, absent or
`null` for none). The inverse of `preset.load`. Refused with `not_found` for an
unknown device or parameter, `invalid` for a value that is not finite, a malformed
`preset` and a device without presets. Undo: `preset.restore_device` with the previous
values and preset.

preset.description: The preset the device shows; absent or `null` for none.

oneOf.description: Built into Faulk, read-only.
In the project's folder: it travels with the project.
In the user's library: available in every project.

PresetRef.description: A preset, by where it lives and its id there.

id.description:
A factory id (`faulk.osc_synth/round-bass`) or, in the project or the library, the
preset's ULID.

ProjectCommand.description: The commands of this domain, tagged by `type`.

oneOf.description:
Rename the project. The name is trimmed, not empty, at most 200 characters.
Undo: rename it back to its previous name.

Open the project folder the host staged under `folder` (the host reads the folder
first; named any other way, the command is refused as `not_staged`), replacing the
current project: the engine starts over from it (stopped, nothing held, the saved solo and
selection restored from `.faulk/session.json`). A folder that is not a valid
project of this version is refused with the reason and nothing changes. Replaces
the history: not undoable, destructive (the caller confirms first when the current
project has unsaved changes).

Start a new project: the page's default one, a single synth track, in no folder yet,
with its own identity. It replaces the current project, its history and its session
(the chosen MIDI input stays); the engine starts over from it. Not undoable, destructive:
the page first keeps the current project's changes where it can (written into its folder,
or kept as a draft in the browser's storage, which stays listed). Only when they cannot
be kept anywhere does it ask the user, whoever sends the command, and nothing changes if
the user cancels. The question is a dialog of the page, so it needs no click. `name`
is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters): without one the project is called
"Sketch" (the page names its drafts by the time they were started, #473).

Write the project to its folder now, without waiting for the automatic save that
follows each change by a moment. A project that has no folder yet asks for one, as
`project.save_as` does. Changes nothing in the project, so it never enters the
history.

Ask the user for the project's name (a field prefilled with the current one), then for
a folder, and write the whole project into a folder of that name inside it; the project
takes that name (a `project.rename`, undoable) and then lives in that folder, and the
automatic save keeps writing there. The name and the folder are chosen by the user (a
browser needs a click for it), so an agent that is not driven by one gets a notice in the
page instead, and nothing is chosen. A folder of that name that already holds files is
refused. The old folder is left as it is. Changes nothing else in the project, so the save
itself never enters the history.

Export the project as a `.faulkpack`, a zip of its folder that any Faulk reads back,
and hand it to the user as a download. It holds the project as it is now, saved or
not, and the media the project refers to. This is how a project kept in the browser
(no folder chosen) is backed up or moved. Changes nothing in the project, so it never
enters the history.

Open a `.faulkpack` the user chooses: its project replaces the current one and is kept
in the browser as a new project of its own (an import never overwrites a project that
is already there). A file is chosen by the user (a browser needs a click for it), so
an agent that is not driven by one gets a notice in the page instead. A file that is
not a valid pack is refused with the reason and nothing changes. The history of the
replaced project is gone; the page asks first when that project has changes that are
not kept anywhere.

Open a `.faulkpack` hosted at `url`: `https`, with no user name or password in it (plain
`http` only to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, and the page takes it only when Faulk
itself runs on this computer). The page downloads it without cookies or credentials,
checks it whole (size, files, format) and opens its project as a new project of its own,
as `project.import_pack` does with a file: kept in the browser's storage where the
browser has one, in the tab alone where it has none. Nothing in the pack runs as code.
When the browser already keeps the project of that pack (the same link opened before), the
page opens the copy it keeps instead of a second one. The current project is never
overwritten: it stays where it is kept (its folder, or the browser), and
`project.list_stored` then `project.open_browser_project` or `project.open_recent` bring
it back; the page asks first when that project has changes that are kept nowhere. A link
that cannot be downloaded, a file that is not a valid pack and a pack that is too big are
refused in the page with a notice, and nothing changes. The result only says the command
was accepted, not how the download ended. Not undoable: opening a project is not an edit
of one; go back to the previous project through the project list.

List the projects this page can open: the folders opened recently (each with an `id`)
and the projects kept in the browser's own storage (each with a `dir`), newest first.
The page reads its storage again before it answers. The `id` and the `dir` are the
names `project.open_recent`, `project.open_browser_project` and
`project.delete_browser_project` take. Changes nothing in the project.

Bring back the project that was open last time, the one the page offers after a reload
(a folder, which asks the browser for its permission again and so needs a click by the
user, or a draft kept in the browser), or the one that the page tried to reopen by itself
and could not (locked by another tab, unreadable): the notice then offers this command
as its retry. A folder still needs the user's click when the browser withdrew its
permission: an agent that is not driven by one gets a notice in the page. Nothing
happens, with a notice, when the page offers nothing. The current project is replaced;
the page asks first when it has changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces
the history.

Choose a project folder and open it, replacing the current project. The folder is
chosen by the user (a browser needs a click for it), so an agent that is not driven by
one gets a notice in the page instead. A folder that is not a project is refused with
the reason and nothing changes. The page asks first when the current project has
changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces the history.

Open a folder from the recent projects, by the `id` that `project.list_stored` gives,
replacing the current project. When the browser withdrew its permission on the folder,
it asks again, which needs a click by the user: an agent that is not driven by one gets
a notice in the page. An `id` the page does not know is refused with a notice. The page
asks first when the current project has changes that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it
replaces the history.

Open a project kept in the browser's storage (a draft, or a project where the browser
has no folders), by the `dir` that `project.list_stored` gives, replacing the current
project. A `dir` the page does not list is refused with a notice, and so is a project
that another tab has open. The page asks first when the current project has changes
that are kept nowhere. Not undoable: it replaces the history.

Delete a project kept in the browser's storage, for good, by the `dir` that
`project.list_stored` gives. The page always asks the user to confirm first, whoever
sends the command, and nothing is deleted until the user says yes. The project that is
open, a project another tab has open and a `dir` the page does not list are refused
with a notice. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user
answered. Not undoable: the files are gone (`project.export_pack` makes a copy first).

When the project's folder was edited outside Faulk while the project has unsaved
changes, keep this page's version: the folder's files are replaced by the project right
away, and the outside edits are lost. The page always asks the user to
confirm first, whoever sends the command. Refused with a notice when the folder is not
in conflict. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user answered.
Changes nothing in the project, so it never enters the history.

When the project's folder was edited outside Faulk while the project has unsaved
changes, take the folder's version: the project is replaced by what the folder holds,
and the changes made since the last write are lost. The page always asks the user to
confirm first, whoever sends the command. Refused with a notice when the folder is not
in conflict. The result only says the command was accepted, not what the user answered.
Not undoable: it replaces the history.

After the browser withdrew the right to write in the project's folder, ask for it
again (the browser shows a prompt, which needs a click by the user: an agent that is
not driven by one gets a notice in the page), then write the changes that waited.
Changes nothing in the project, so it never enters the history.

Measure how loud the song is without playing it nor writing a file: the same
offline render as `project.export_audio` (the engine that plays the song, run
faster than real time), but only the levels come back, per track and for the
master, so an agent without ears learns whether its song sounds, whether it is too
loud, and whether a track is silent. The range is the whole song by default, or
bars `from_bar` to `to_bar` (both, counted from 1, the last one included); the
tail after the range is not measured. Levels are in dBFS (0 is full scale), `null`
is silence; a peak is the larger of the two channels, an RMS the power mean of
both, over the whole range (not the loudest short window that `mixer.levels`
gives). The metronome and the loop are off, the solo and mute state are on. Audio
clips are measured as they play: the render reads their files from the project's
folder, and a file that cannot be read leaves its clip silent. Refused, as an export
is, when there is nothing to render (empty arrangement, a range that starts after
the end of the arrangement or is out of order), and when the range lasts more than
10 minutes (a `limit` error). The page runs the render in the background (a few
seconds for a few minutes of music), one at a time; it answers `unavailable` when
another analysis runs or the page's engine is not ready. A query: changes nothing
in the project and never enters the history.

Render the project to an audio file (WAV) and save it, offline: the same engine
that plays the song, run faster than real time, so the file is the song as it
sounds, not a recording of the speakers. `region` is `song` (default: from bar 1
to the end of the last placement of the arrangement, then the tail, so that an
effect such as the echo rings out; the file ends where the sound falls under
-90 dBFS, after 30 seconds at most), `loop` (the loop region once, then the same
tail) or `bars` (from the start of bar `from_bar` to the end of bar `to_bar`, both
counted from 1, required with it and refused without it, the last one included,
then the same tail). `bit_depth` is `pcm16`, `pcm24` (default) or `float32`;
`sample_rate` is 44100, 48000 (default) or 96000. The metronome is never in the
file; the solo and mute state are. Audio clips are in the file as they play: the
render reads their files from the project's folder, in the page in both modes (so in
Boost too, where they are not heard yet), and waits for each read; a file that cannot
be read leaves its clips silent and the page names it when the render ends. It is
refused when there is
nothing to render (empty arrangement, no loop region for `loop`, a `bars` range that

oneOf.description:
Change the settings of recording; every field is optional and a field left out stays
as it is. `offset_ms` (-500 to 500): every recorded note is moved this much earlier,
on top of the output latency the host estimates (negative: later). `replace`: a take
removes, in the clip it writes into, the notes that start in the range it recorded
(from its first note to the end of its last), instead of adding to them (overdub,
the default). `quantize_on_input` (`none`, `quarter`, `eighth`, `sixteenth`,
`thirty-second`, `eighth-triplet`, `sixteenth-triplet`; default `none`) and
`quantize_strength` (0 to 100 percent, default 100): the starts of the take's own
notes are moved toward that grid of the clip when `record.commit_take` writes the
take, never the notes the clip already had, and never their lengths. They belong to
the machine, so they are session state: saved with the session, never in the
project, and not undoable. A take uses the settings at the moment it is written, unless `record.commit_take` is given its own.

Start recording the armed MIDI tracks (`track.arm`); refused when none is armed or
when a take is still waiting to be committed. `target`: `{"at": "scene", "scene":
<id>}` (the launch grid: overdub into the cell's clip, or a new clip in an empty
cell) or `{"at": "arrangement"}` (the default: each note where it is played). From a
stopped transport it plays from the play position, after the metronome's count-in
bars (heard, not recorded), and with a scene target it launches that scene's clip
of each armed track first; on a running transport it records at once. `latency_ms`
is the output latency the host estimates (0 to 1000, default 0). The notes come
back from the engine; `record.stop` ends the take, which the host then writes with
`record.commit_take`, one history entry. Not undoable itself.

End the capture of the running take; the transport keeps playing. The notes still
held are cut here. The host writes the take with `record.commit_take` once the
engine has returned its last notes (within one report, about 33 ms). Does nothing
when no take is recording. Not undoable itself.

Drop the current take without writing anything (undo during a take): the capture
stops if it runs. Does nothing when there is no take. Not undoable: it wrote nothing.

Write a take into the project, every track at once, as **one** history entry. Per
track, `notes` are the notes as played: `start` in transport ticks, `length` in
ticks. Every start is first moved `shift_ms` earlier at the project's tempo; when the
transport loops and the start is inside the loop, the move wraps round the loop (a note
that would go before the loop's start comes from its end). With a
scene target, a cell that holds a clip takes the notes on top of its own (overdub):
a note lands where the clip played at that moment, from `anchor` (the transport tick
of the clip's position 0) or else from the bar of the first note, round its loop;
a clip without a loop grows to the bar after the last note. An empty cell gets a new
clip from the bar of the first note to the bar after the last one (at least one
bar), looping over its length. With the arrangement target, a note inside a
placement goes into its clip where the placement shows it; the other notes make one
new clip per gap between placements, from the bar of its first note to the bar after
its last, cut at the next placement. A note before tick 0 or before its clip is
dropped and counted; a note longer than its clip is cut at the clip's end. With
`replace` on (`record.set_settings`), a clip that takes notes first loses the notes
that start in the range the track recorded (its first note to the end of its last),
counted in `replaced`. With `quantize_on_input` on, the starts of the take's notes
move toward the grid of their clip by `quantize_strength` (a note stays inside its
clip, lengths never change). Undo: `record.restore` puts the clips back as they
were, replaced notes included. `replace`, `quantize_on_input` and `quantize_strength`
override the session's settings (`record.set_settings`) for this write only; left out,
the session's apply.

Create a scene at the end of the launch grid. `name` is optional (trimmed, at most

arrangement. Not destructive: undo brings everything back. A clip that is playing
stops sounding when its notes are released. Undo: `scene.restore` brings the scene
and its clips back with their identifiers and position.

Bring a deleted scene back with its identifier, its name, its position and the
clips of its slots, as `scene.delete` removed it: the inverse of a delete. Refused
when the scene's identifier or any identifier inside it is already in use, at the

skip, 0 by default) and `limit` (scenes to return, 1 to 1000, 100 by default; any

oneOf.description:
Create a track at the end of the list: `kind` is `midi` or `audio`. A MIDI track
plays `instrument`, the type id of a built-in instrument (`faulk.osc_synth`, the
default); an audio track plays the clip player and takes no `instrument`. `name`
is optional (trimmed, at most 200 characters; empty by default) and so is `color`
(`#rrggbb`; by default the first of the sixteen palette hues no track has yet, stored
with the track so that it never changes when other tracks move). Refused with `limit` only at the project's safety limit of tracks.
Undo: `track.delete`.

the solo, the arming and the monitoring of the track are cleared (session state,
not restored by undo: an undone delete brings the track back unarmed). Undo:
`track.restore` brings the whole track back with its identifiers and position.

inverse of a delete. `snapshot` is the whole track: its order key, mixer,
devices, clips, placements and automation. Refused when the track's identifier or
any identifier inside it is already in use, at the safety limit of tracks, or when
the snapshot is not a valid track of the project. Undo: `track.delete`.

means last. Refused with `invalid` when the tracks around that position share an

Replace a MIDI track's instrument by another instrument of the registry: `instrument`
is the type id of a built-in instrument (`faulk.osc_synth`, `faulk.drums`). The new
device starts at its default settings under a new identifier and takes the old
one's place first in the chain; the effects stay. The old instrument's settings are
lost unless undone. Choosing the instrument the track already plays changes
nothing. The automation lanes that target the old instrument go with it (lead's
decision on #380; the output counts them in `removed_lanes`, so that the interface
can say so) and come back with it on undo, in the same history entry. Refused on an
audio track (it plays the clip player) and for a type that is not an instrument.

identifier, settings and lanes.

`track.set_instrument`. `current` is the instrument in the track now, replaced by

when `current` is not the track's instrument, or when the snapshot is not an
instrument that fits the track (a built-in device must be one of the registry; a
module device is taken as it is). The lanes that target `current` are removed with
it; `lanes` (absent: none) are the lanes that targeted the instrument put back, as
`track.set_instrument` took them out: each must target the restored instrument and
a parameter it has, under an identifier not in use. Undo: the same swap the other

oneOf.description:

controllers) reaches the armed tracks as well as the selected one, and recording

the project. Refused with `not_found` for a track that does not exist, except to

track's instrument sounds what is played whatever this says; it matters for the
audio input. Refused with `not_found` for a track that does not exist, except to
stop monitoring a track deleted since.

key), with new identifiers for the track, its
devices, clips, placements and automation lanes. The clips are new, independent
clips with the same content and the same names.
`name` is optional (trimmed, at most 200
characters): the copy has the source's name and colour by default
(recolour it with `track.set_color`). The copy is never muted
(volume and pan are copied); solo and arming are session state of the source and
are not copied. Refused with `limit` at

the copy.

oneOf.description:
Start playback from the playhead: the marker (the last `transport.seek`, the start
of the project at first), or where `transport.pause` left it.

the start of the project at first), so the position shown is the one
`transport.play` restarts from. Sent again with the playhead already on the marker,
it goes back to the start of the project (tick 0) and the marker with it. To stay
where the playhead is, use `transport.pause`. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Pause playback at `tick`, the playhead position (960 ticks per quarter note), from 0
to 2^40: playback stops there and `transport.play` resumes from there, while the
marker (the last `transport.seek`) stays where it was, so `transport.stop` still
brings the playhead back to it. Played live: not undoable, not saved.

Set the project's tempo in BPM, from 20 to 999. A value outside the range or not
a number is refused, and so is a tempo at which an audio placement (whose length is
in frames of its file, so its end in ticks follows the tempo) would end past 2^40.
A faster tempo lengthens audio placements in ticks, so one may then reach into the
next placement of its track: the project allows it, and the later one plays from its
start. Undo: set the previous tempo back.

Set the project's time signature: numerator 1 to 32, denominator a power of two
from 1 to 32 (4 and 4 is common time). Anything else is refused. Undo: set the

Set the launch quantization, global to the project: the grid a clip or scene launch
snaps to. One of `none` (at once), `sixteenth`, `beat`, `bar`, `bars_2`, `bars_4`,
`bars_8`; a project starts at `bar`. Any other value is refused. Undo: set the
previous value back.

2^40`, or `null` for none. This does not turn the loop on (see
`transport.toggle_loop`), unless `enabled` says so; clearing the region while the
loop is on turns the loop off too. `enabled` (optional) turns the loop on or off
with the region: on without a region is refused. Undo: set the previous region
back, and the loop switch when the command changed it.

Turn the loop over the loop region on or off. Turning it on without a region is
refused. A setting of the project: saved with it, listed in the history's activity
log, but not undoable (undo and redo leave the switch as it is).

Change the metronome: `enabled` (click on or off), `gain_db` (level, -96 to +6,
`null` for silence) and `count_in_bars` (bars counted in before recording, 0 to 16). Every field is
optional and a missing one is left as it is; at least one is required. A value
outside its range is refused. A setting of the project: saved with it, listed in
the history's activity log, but not undoable.

stateless call for `AGENT_IDLE` (`crates/helper`). Its last session ended when the client
closed it, when the stdio bridge's input ended, or after `AGENT_IDLE` without a request.

closes the history group that agent (`agent:<agent>`) left open, ends its turn and
withdraws its questions to the user. Sent on the session and on every control link.
